findings.title: Push-ingest authentication is absent from the machine-readable security contract
findings.what: The operation description states that POST /api/ingest/{sourceId}/artifacts requires ingest authentication, but the operation has no `security` declaration and `components.securitySchemes` defines only CSRF, enterprise Bearer, and Basic authentication. Because top-level `security` is empty, OpenAPI tooling interprets this write endpoint as unauthenticated and cannot discover or supply its required credential. The documented responses also omit the authentication failure response.
findings.fix: Define the ingest Bearer-token security scheme, attach it to POST /api/ingest/{sourceId}/artifacts, and document its 401 response. Keep the existing CSRF scheme separate because cross-origin shippers use a dedicated credential.
findings.acceptance: Parse the OpenAPI document and assert that POST /api/ingest/{sourceId}/artifacts has a nonempty security requirement referencing a defined ingest Bearer scheme and includes a 401 response; generated clients must expose a way to configure that credential.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the operation has no local `security` key and the components section has no ingest scheme. The smallest related baseline handler comparison confirmed authentication is actually enforced with a dedicated shared Bearer token and returns 401 on failure, so this is a surviving machine-readable contract defect rather than a runtime authentication bypass.
